editorial:
If you loved the first film, you will feel right at home with Max and his furry friends. This time around, Max is dealing with big life changes when his owner gets married and brings home a baby. The family heads to the countryside, where Max faces cows, foxes, and a scary turkey. Meanwhile, back in the city, Gidget tries to rescue Max's favorite toy from a cat-filled apartment, and Snowball goes on a rescue mission. The movie splits into three storylines that eventually come together. It is bright, colorful, and packed with silly animal jokes that kids will love.

The voice cast is solid, with Harrison Ford stealing scenes as the gruff farm dog Rooster. The animation looks great, especially the countryside scenes. On the downside, the three separate plots feel a bit scattered, and the pacing can drag in spots. Still, the humor lands more often than not, and the heart is there. This is a great pick for families with young kids or anyone wanting a light, feel-good watch.
endingExplained: In the final act, Max finally stands up to the scary turkey and learns to be brave thanks to Rooster's tough love. Snowball and Daisy rescue a tiger from an abusive circus owner, and Gidget successfully retrieves Max's toy from the cat apartment. The three storylines merge when everyone reunites. Max returns home more confident, no longer afraid of the world. The movie ends on a warm note with Max embracing his new role as a protective big brother to the baby.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves animated family comedies with lovable animal characters.
